See whether every permission is working
What Focuno reads, and what it never does

Focuno works entirely on your phone. It has no accounts, no analytics and no internet permission, so nothing about you can leave this device. Your usage history lives in a private database on this phone and is deleted when you uninstall.

Which app is in front of you, and how long each app is used. If you choose to block only Reels or Shorts, Focuno also checks a few technical screen-part names inside Instagram or YouTube to see whether the video screen is open. That check only happens while such a rule exists and one of those apps is open.

Messages, photos, passwords, text on screen, usernames, captions, your location, contacts, or anything you type in other apps. The only text Focuno keeps is the reason you give when you ask to unlock an app, and that stays on this phone.

Android locks this switch for apps installed from a file instead of the Play Store. It is a safety rule, and you can unlock it yourself in about a minute:
Tap the greyed-out Focuno once in the Accessibility list. Android says \"Restricted setting\". Tap OK.
Come back here and tap the button below to open Focuno\'s app info.
Tap the three dots in the top right corner, then tap Allow restricted settings and confirm.
Go back to Accessibility, tap Focuno and switch it on.
No three dots, or no Allow restricted settings? Do step 1 again first. The menu only appears after Android has shown that message.
These settings stop your phone from quietly shutting Focuno down. Exact names vary a little between software versions.
Open Settings, then Apps, then Manage apps, then Focuno.
Turn on Autostart, and set Battery saver to No restrictions.
In the recent apps screen, press and hold Focuno and tap the lock icon.
Open Settings, then Apps, then App management, then Focuno.
Under Battery usage, choose Allow background activity.
Open Settings, then Battery, then Background power consumption management.
Find Focuno and choose Allow high background power consumption.
Open i Manager, then App manager, then Autostart, and turn Focuno on.
Open Settings, then Battery, then Battery optimization, then Focuno.
Open Settings, then Apps, then Focuno, and allow auto-launch and background activity.
Open Settings, then Battery, then Background usage limits.
Add Focuno to Never sleeping apps.
Open Settings, then Apps, then Focuno, then Battery, and choose Unrestricted.
Open Settings, then Apps, then Focuno, then Battery.
Choose Unrestricted (or Don\'t optimize) and allow background activity.
If your phone has an Autostart or App launch setting, turn it on for Focuno.
Focuno helps you stop doomscrolling while you prepare for GATE, JEE, NEET or UPSC. It counts your screen time honestly, pauses the apps you choose, and adds a short pause before you open them.
No account, no ads, no internet access.
Setup takes about two minutes. Each step explains why it is needed.
Android calls this Usage access. Focuno uses it to count your time and to notice when you open an app you want paused. It never sees what you do inside apps.
Focuno can already pause apps without this. Turning on Accessibility makes it react faster and lets it block only Reels or Shorts. If Android says it is restricted, you can skip this step.
Focuno draws a calm pause screen on top of a blocked app. This permission is what lets it appear over other apps.
Some phones close background apps to save battery, and that also switches blocking off. Allow notifications so Focuno can warn you if that happens, and ask Android not to optimise Focuno.
One last step for your phone
Phone makers add their own battery managers that can stop apps in the background. Follow the steps below for your phone so Focuno stays on.
We guessed from popular apps. Switch on the ones you want Focuno to help you with. You can change this any time.
Choose when these apps should pause. You can add more times, or different ones for each app, later.
Pick at least one app on the previous step to create a schedule.
Blocking adds friction, not a lock: you can still unlock an app with a short wait and a reason. Android does not allow an app to be made unbypassable.

Compare Focuno with Android Settings, app by app

Android Settings counts every app except your home screen and the system bar. Focuno now does the same, including time spent inside Focuno. If the totals still differ by more than a couple of minutes, take a screenshot of this screen.
